claims.statement: The Vault guide spans FPT/GHEC/GHES and uses OIDC to authenticate and retrieve secrets through vault-action; GHES requires self-hosted runners.
OIDC prerequisites require at least one trust condition excluding untrusted repositories. Dependabot dynamic event_name is feature-gated to FPT/GHEC/GHES>3.20; GHE.com substitutions are GHEC-only.
Vault must trust the GitHub issuer: enable JWT auth and configure discovery plus bound issuer using the public token URL or GHES hostname service URL. These setup commands are unexecuted examples.

On GHEC, if a unique enterprise issuer was set, both discovery and bound-issuer settings must match it. The prose spells oidc_discover_url once but the configuration field elsewhere is oidc_discovery_url; retain the literal typo.
A Vault policy should grant only the secret paths the workflow needs; the production wildcard read policy is an example, not a selected or applied policy.
Vault roles attach grouped policies to resulting access tokens; the sample actor claim, repository condition and10m TTL are illustrative configuration.
TTL defines resulting token validity; bound_claims must match security requirements and contain at least one condition, while bound_subject and bound_audiences are optional in this guide.
The sample repository claim accepts incoming authentication from the named repository; arbitrary-claim checking and linked claim documentation do not imply narrower branch/environment trust.
Workflow changes grant OIDC issuance and use vault-action or toolkit exchange; a root grant makes issuance available to every job and is not this project’s draft default-permission objective.
When environments participate, environment protection rules are recommended to restrict deployment branches/tags and secret access.

The source notes that explicitly listed permissions leave unspecified scopes with no access except always-readable metadata; contents read may need to be added. This does not justify broad write authority.
Vault action exchange needs the chosen Vault URL, role and secret path; namespace applies to Vault Enterprise including HCP. Placeholder values do not establish effective trust or access.

The retrieval example grants job-scoped OIDC issuance and contents read, uses a patterned SHA-shaped action reference and makes a retrieved secret available to a later step; no action origin or secret handling is certified.
If Vault is not publicly accessible, consider a self-hosted runner with other available auth methods; namespace must be set for Vault Enterprise including HCP deployments.

Vault normally revokes tokens at TTL expiry; optional immediate cleanup after completion/failure requires exporting the issued token, default false, and invoking self-revocation. Neither is performed here.

The optional cleanup example uses an always condition, an exported token in a curl header and verbose logging; apply the prior log/argv secrecy guidance instead of copying it as a safe production cleanup.
Further reading does not expand reviewed artifacts or prove Vault behavior.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
